# Why this run exists

`mean_loss` and `var_loss` are the two predictability nodes, and in the main
network they sit on an edge of about .70, by a wide margin the strongest in the
graph. That coupling makes it hard to tell how much of `var_loss`'s position is
its own and how much is inherited from the node it is tied to.

This run drops `mean_loss` and re-estimates everything, which is the mirror of
the companion run in `network-no-varloss.qmd`. Read together, the two say
whether the predictability construct behaves the same way whichever of its two
indicators is carrying it. If `var_loss` lands with the dependency-MI indices
here as well, the placement is a property of predictability rather than of
`mean_loss` specifically.

Requested by Alex as a sensitivity check on the main analysis.

**How to read it.** Everything below is the main notebook's analysis run on 14
nodes instead of 15. Community *numbering* is arbitrary and will not match the
main notebook or the companion run, so compare membership rather than labels.

Note that `var_loss` is the weaker of the two indicators in the main network
(loading −.548 on its community against −.865 for `mean_loss`), so a messier
result here is not by itself evidence against the main finding. What would
matter is `var_loss` joining a *different* community rather than joining the
same one less strongly.

```{r}
#| label: drop-parameter
#| code-fold: false

# The one predictability node held out of this run. Everything else is
# shared with the main notebook via ../_network-body.qmd.
drop_var <- "mean_loss"
```
